summary: v3 testing of Spring Boot + PostgreSQL backend + React frontend. Backend pytest: 20/20 passed via internal/localhost. Frontend: COMPLETELY BLOCKED — login (and every browser API call) fails with 403 'Invalid CORS request' because Spring Security CORS rejects the configured allowed origin when sent from the browser with credentials. Confirmed reproducible with curl when Origin header is added. WebSocket via public URL also returns 403 (handshake then CORS rejection). Backend tests pass only because requests go without an Origin header.

critical.issue: Returns 403 'Invalid CORS request' whenever Origin header is set to the configured allowed origin (e.g., https://parlance-dev.preview.emergentagent.com). Reproduced via curl: `curl -X POST https://.../api/auth/login -H 'Origin: https://parlance-dev.preview.emergentagent.com' -d '{...}'` -> 403 'Invalid CORS request'. Without Origin header, returns 200. This breaks the entire frontend (login fails immediately, no chat, no WS).
Public WSS handshake returns 403 Forbidden (Spring Security headers in response). Likely same CORS issue propagating to the WebSocket upgrade. Internal ws://localhost:8001 works fine.

Returns 403 with empty body instead of 401. Root cause: SecurityConfig has no explicit AuthenticationEntryPoint, so Spring Security defaults to Http403ForbiddenEntryPoint. ResponseStatusException(UNAUTHORIZED) thrown by AuthService is not propagating because the request appears to be blocked at the security filter chain level for unauthenticated paths in some cases, or the entry point overrides the controller's status. Frontend cannot distinguish between 'wrong password' and 'forbidden'.

After 5 failed attempts the controller throws ResponseStatusException(TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, 429) but client receives 403. Cannot verify brute-force protection works. Likely same root cause as above (no proper exception handler/entry point).

minor.issue: Returns 201 Created (correct REST). Old test_parlance.py assertions for 200 were tightened to accept 201 — informational, not a backend bug.

integration_issues.issue: POST /api/auth/login returns 403 'Invalid CORS request'. Frontend shows 'Invalid email or password' (its generic 4xx message). User can never log in via UI even with correct admin credentials.
WSS upgrade to /api/ws?token=... returns 403. No realtime messages, presence, or typing indicators will ever work in production frontend until CORS+WS handshake is fixed.

action_items: FIX CORS (CRITICAL): In /app/springboot/src/main/java/com/parlance/config/SecurityConfig.java, replace `config.setAllowedOrigins(Arrays.asList(corsOrigins.split(',')))` with `config.setAllowedOriginPatterns(Arrays.asList(corsOrigins.split(',')))` OR additionally trim each origin: `Arrays.stream(corsOrigins.split(',')).map(String::trim).toList()`. Verify `cors.checkOrigin(...)` does not return null for the configured origin. After fix, run: `curl -X POST https://parlance-dev.preview.emergentagent.com/api/auth/login -H 'Origin: https://parlance-dev.preview.emergentagent.com' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@parlance.com","password":"Admin1234!"}'` and expect 200.

FIX 401/429 PROPAGATION: Configure a custom AuthenticationEntryPoint that returns 401 with JSON body, OR add a @ControllerAdvice/@RestControllerAdvice handler for ResponseStatusException that bypasses Spring Security's default Http403ForbiddenEntryPoint. Currently every unauthenticated/invalid-creds/rate-limit response collapses to 403 with empty body.

VERIFY WEBSOCKET AFTER CORS FIX: After CORS fix, test `wss://parlance-dev.preview.emergentagent.com/api/ws?token=<jwt>`. WS handler accepts (sec-websocket-accept header is present in the failed response), but Spring Security blocks the response with 403. Ensure /api/ws is also CORS-friendly and Spring Security permits WS upgrade.
REBUILD JAR after Java fix: `cd /app/springboot && ./mvnw -DskipTests package` then `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` (wait ~12s).
(carry-over from iteration_1) Investigate duplicate message rendering in ChatContext WS handler (couldn't retest because login is broken).
critical_code_review_comments: SecurityConfig CORS is broken at runtime even though configuration looks correct on paper. Reproduce: curl with `Origin: https://parlance-dev.preview.emergentagent.com` returns 'Invalid CORS request'. Likely Spring 6 + allowCredentials=true requires `setAllowedOriginPatterns` or there is whitespace/encoding issue in the .properties value being split.
No AuthenticationEntryPoint configured -> all unauthenticated 401s collapse to 403 empty body. Frontend cannot give meaningful errors and rate-limiting (429) is invisible.

AuthService.login uses request.getRemoteAddr() for brute-force identifier — behind ingress this is the proxy IP (shared by all users), so a single attacker could lock out other users on the same email. Consider using X-Forwarded-For with a trust list.
test_parlance.py had a return value warning (returns msg id from test_send_message_to_channel). Should remove the return.
WebSocketConfig uses setAllowedOrigins('*') — fine for now but not consistent with the strict CORS list in SecurityConfig.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Critical blocker: Spring Security CORS rejects the configured allowed origin with 'Invalid CORS request' (403) whenever the browser sends Origin header. After E1 fixes SecurityConfig.corsConfigurationSource() (likely replace setAllowedOrigins with setAllowedOriginPatterns and/or trim split values), re-run: 1) `curl -H 'Origin: https://parlance-dev.preview.emergentagent.com' -X POST .../api/auth/login` should be 200; 2) playwright login flow should redirect to /chat; 3) WSS handshake should succeed. Also need to add an AuthenticationEntryPoint so 401/429 reach the client correctly. Backend pytest 20/20 already passes (it doesn't send Origin header so masks the bug).
rca_of_issue: Spring Boot 3.2 + Spring Security 6 with allowCredentials=true + setAllowedOrigins(exactList) is likely returning null from CorsConfiguration.checkOrigin(...) for the supplied origin, which DefaultCorsProcessor renders as 'Invalid CORS request' with status 403. Possible reasons: (a) the property value being split into a list contains a hidden character or trailing whitespace, (b) Spring 6 + credentials path now prefers setAllowedOriginPatterns. Fix in SecurityConfig: use setAllowedOriginPatterns and/or .map(String::trim) on the split result. Reproduction: `curl -i -X POST https://parlance-dev.preview.emergentagent.com/api/auth/login -H 'Origin: https://parlance-dev.preview.emergentagent.com' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@parlance.com","password":"Admin1234!"}'` -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden, body 'Invalid CORS request'.
